## Problem
When using NVM (Node Version Manager), the standard installation and usage instructions for MCP servers don't work. The app tries to use an incorrect Node and fails.

## Workaround

1. Avoid `npx`, install packages globally.
2. Use absolute paths to both the Node executable and server script.

Example:

```json
{  
  "mcpServers": {
    "puppeteer": {
      "command": "/Users/username/.nvm/versions/node/v22.11.0/bin/node",
      "args": [
        "/Users/username/.nvm/versions/node/v22.11.0/lib/node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/server-puppeteer/dist/index.js"
items.title: MCP Servers Don't Work with NVM

- "China Standard Time" -> "Asia/Shanghai"

We could:
1. Add a mapping dictionary for common Windows time zone names
2. Try the provided time zone name first, if failed:

items.author: xianminx
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Currently, the `McpServer` implementation in the ModelContextProtocol likely handles client connections in a one-to-one manner. This means that only a single client can be actively communicating with the server at any given time. This limitation can be problematic in scenarios where multiple entities need to interact with the ModelContextProtocol server concurrently. For instance, in applications with multiple users or independent processes that need to access the server's functionalities, the current single-connection mode
items.title: Support for multiple clients in McpServer
